questions.question: What source did Mike use for his definition?

analyses.content: 录音中男生明确指出他引用了去年研究方法课上老师发的讲义（handout）里的定义。
你可能会因为听到录音后半部分提到的历史学家用来写学术文章（academic articles）而误选B，但这其实指的是口述历史的用处而不是定义的来源。
But first, how do you define oral history? Well, in fact, I used the definition you gave us last year in our research methodology class. I found the handout in my file.

options.optionContent: wide access to the interviews by the public

questions.question: According to Mike and his tutor, what is the most important contribution of the internet to oral history?

analyses.content: 男生反驳了老师的观点，指出互联网的真正贡献在于能让采访录音被永久保存（preserved forever）。
你可能会被前面老师提到的“大量人能访问”（选项C）或“更多学生感兴趣”（选项B）带跑偏，但录音通过转折词“But”强调了“永久保存”才是最重要的贡献。

I was also interested in how the Internet has contributed to oral history studies. Yes, it means that lots of people can access the material, and that's great. Also, the interactive nature of the better websites means that more students get interested in oral history. But from what I've read, the real contribution of the Internet is that the recording of the interviews will be preserved forever. In the old days, the tapes would just wear out, and after some years, you couldn't really use them, but not now.

questions.question: Mike says he chose his particular topic because

analyses.content: 男生坦言自己甚至不太喜欢足球，但由于他的爸爸是个狂热粉丝（huge fan）能帮到他，所以才选了这个主题。
录音中提到他的朋友们觉得他选这个主题很疯狂（crazy），而不是鼓励他，所以千万别只听到 friends 就顺手选了C。

Why did you decide to study a sports team? Well, actually, I don't even like football very much. [laughs] And some of my friends think I'm crazy to go for that subject, but my dad is a huge fan, and he might be able to help me.

questions.question: What does Mike say was his best source of information about the team?

analyses.content: 男生说他在镇报社办公室看了所有旧新闻报道，并明确表示那才是他获得最有帮助信息的地方（most helpful information）。
你可能会因为听到了球队经理（team manager）和当地图书馆（local library）而纠结，但联系经理只是帮他找到了人，而图书馆没保留太多记录，都不是最佳信息源。

And how did you find out background about the team? You talked to the team manager, I assume. Yes, I did manage to track him down, and I looked at all the old news stories about the team in the town newspaper office. That was where I got the most helpful information. I had high hopes that the local library would have lots of stuff, but they don't keep many records for more than ten years.

questions.question: How did Mike find the former players he has arranged to interview?

analyses.content: 导师和男生确认了他是用一种老派方法，也就是只通过电话簿（telephone directory）找到了这些前队员。
录音中明确否定了使用网站（Not a website），男生也补充说甚至不需要用当地球队的记录（didn't even need to use the local team's records），听到这两个否定就可以直接排除A和B。

I know that you managed to locate ten of the original eighteen members of the team using an old-fashioned method, didn't you? Not a website or anything, just the telephone directory. Yes. I didn't even need to use the local team's records.

Aspects of the proposed interviews

analyses.content: 导师评价男生起草的问题作为口头提问来说有些过于复杂了（rather complex），这完美同义替换了选项G的太复杂（too complicated）。
由于导师紧接着说“You don't have too many”，说明问题数量并不算多，所以千万别凭感觉选代表数量太多或太长的干扰项。

I've read through the list of questions you've drafted. I felt most of them are rather complex to be processed as oral questions. You don't have too many, which is good, but you should try to do something about that problem. Right. I'll work on them.
导师明确指出男生给每次采访安排了太多的时间（too much time），并建议采访应该紧凑些，直接对应选项D的时间太长（too long）。
你可能会漏听“too much time”，但紧接着老师说希望采访紧凑点（tight）、不要没完没了（not going on and on），由此也能稳稳反推出时间给得太长了这个核心问题。
And the time you've allotted for each interview, actually, I think you may have scheduled too much time for each. You want them to be tight, not going on and on. That makes for better results.
男生抱怨自己的旧录音机有时候就是不工作（doesn't seem to work），甚至在和他爸爸试录时死机了，说明设备非常不可靠（too unreliable）。
录音中男生用“without”否定了噪音大（noise），又用“isn't”否定了复杂（complicated），如果你没听到否定词就极容易掉进选项C和G的陷阱。

One thing I'm nervous about is the recording equipment I use. I've got an old recorder. It runs without making too much noise, and it isn't complicated, but it sometimes just doesn't seem to work. Mm. It stopped during an interview I tried out with my dad.
导师担心男生选的主题太笼统了（quite general），不够具体（not very specific），这完美对应了选项H的太模糊（too vague）。
当听到“general”和“not very specific”时你必须迅速在脑海中将其与选项“vague”进行连线，如果死等原词出现就会彻底跟丢这道题。

Now, I'm a little concerned with the subjects you've chosen to cover. The topics seem quite general, not very specific. For example, why did they like playing for this team? Hmm. You need to talk about more exact things and feelings. That way, your results will be more valuable.
男生原本的报告计划只是单纯记录队员说了什么、发生了什么（what happened），导师要求他加入自己的评价，说明原计划太过客观罗列事实（too factual）。
你可能会因为男生提到了很多个“what”就觉得内容太长或太复杂，但这其实只是在反映他像流水账一样罗列事实，缺乏主观分析（evaluation）。

And you know, the plan for my report seems to be just to report back more or less what the players say, what happened, when, what they each did, and so on. But I'm not sure about that. Yes. Although your outline seems long enough, change it to indicate that you plan to include your own evaluation of the data you get from your interviewees.
